aboutHero: I take ideas apart, figure out how the pieces fit, and build software that works for people.
about: I'm Isack Lugata, a backend and applied AI engineer based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. My Computer Science studies at the University of Dar es Salaam have taken me into APIs, intelligent assistants, infrastructure, and the practical work of turning an idea into a useful system.

I co-founded Ecofy Africa, where we're building agricultural intelligence for smallholder farmers. Working on a product has taught me to look beyond the code: who will use it, what information they need, and how the system fits the way they already work.

My work spans backend development, retrieval-augmented generation, document processing, and deployment. I also lead the 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab at UDSM CoICT, where software meets physical computing and experimentation.

I work with founders and teams who need a backend, an AI feature, or an integration built with care. Outside the terminal: chess, basketball, video editing, and the occasional experiment that starts with 'what if?'.

projects.name: Ecofy Africa
projects.summary: Ecofy Africa is an agricultural intelligence platform for smallholder farmers in Tanzania. As co-founder, CEO and AI Lead, I contribute to the AI services and technical product direction, working with a team to turn farm information into useful decisions.
story: Smallholder farmers need information they can act on, in a form that fits their context. At Ecofy Africa, that means thinking about local users, their growing seasons, and the gap between collecting data and making a useful recommendation.

My contribution focuses on applied AI and backend services: agricultural analysis, conversational assistance, document extraction, and the architecture behind a crop journey that can change as new events happen on a farm. This is a team product; I do not claim sole ownership of the platform.

The work brings together Python services, a React PWA, PostgreSQL, Gemini integration, and agricultural data. The planning direction is event-driven: update crop state when something changes, then revisit the plan rather than follow a fixed checklist.
Building Ecofy has made research and product judgment part of my engineering practice. The next question is not just whether a feature works, but whether it helps a farmer make a better decision.

projects.name: Wakili Msomi
projects.summary: Wakili Msomi explores how retrieval and conversational AI can make Tanzanian legal information easier to navigate in English and Swahili. My involvement began during practical training at Bluefin Solutions, in collaboration with Sheria Kiganjani.
story: Legal information is difficult to navigate when it is scattered across documents or written in unfamiliar language. This project explores a bilingual assistant for finding and working with relevant Tanzanian legal information.

The engineering focus is the connection between document retrieval and a useful response: processing source material, finding relevant context, and presenting an answer in English or Swahili. It is an information assistant, not a substitute for professional legal advice.

My contribution sits in backend and AI development during practical training. The broader system discussions covered document handling, authentication, conversation history, and language-model integration. Exact implementation attribution still needs a final review.

projects.name: Multi-tenant RAG
projects.summary: A retrieval backend for knowledge-aware AI assistants, with separate document collections and configurable assistant behavior. The focus is document ingestion, tenant isolation, and bringing the right context into a language-model response.
story: An assistant becomes more useful when it can work with an organization's own information. The challenge is to make documents searchable while keeping one tenant's knowledge separate from another's.

The ingestion workflow takes source documents, extracts their text, splits it into chunks, and indexes it for semantic retrieval. At query time, the system retrieves relevant context before asking a language model to respond.
The technical direction uses Python, Weaviate, LangChain, and model APIs. Configurable assistant behavior and optional citations make the retrieval layer adaptable to different knowledge collections.

My focus is the backend and AI workflow: how material enters the system, how it is separated, and how retrieved context reaches the assistant. The diagram shows the conceptual flow, not a production benchmark.
[CONFIRM] Repository sharing permission and current deployment status. There are no claims here about organizations served, production throughput, or measured retrieval quality.

projects.name: EnergyOpt
projects.summary: An energy-data analysis workflow that turns uploaded electrical measurements into structured information for dashboards. The backend work centers on file ingestion, column mapping, normalization, and analysis over time.
story: Raw electrical data is not immediately useful. Files arrive with different column names and formats, and measurements need to be mapped and normalized before they can support meaningful analysis.

The backend workflow handles CSV and spreadsheet ingestion, maps timestamp and measurement columns, and prepares data for hourly, daily, and weekly views. The goal is to make consumption patterns and periods of high demand easier to inspect.
[CONFIRM] Current demo, deployment status, and the final database configuration. This is backend and analytics development; commercial use and measurable energy savings have not been verified.

projects.name: Marketplace systems
projects.summary: Backend work and system planning for marketplace products: seller roles, product operations, inventory, and local payment workflows. The focus is on clear permissions, useful APIs, and transaction tracking for Tanzanian businesses.
story: A marketplace connects several different workflows: what a customer sees, what a seller manages, and what an administrator needs to reconcile. A useful backend keeps those responsibilities clear.

My work has included product-management APIs, seller and administrator roles, authentication, and payment-integration planning. Local payment and messaging requirements shape the design alongside the core commerce data model.
Related exploration includes ClickPesa, Selcom, Beem SMS, and fiscal-receipt requirements. These are separate integration contexts, not a claim that one completed platform already runs every service.

projects.name: Infrastructure & DevOps
projects.summary: Deploying and operating applications with Docker, nginx, PostgreSQL, and Linux. This work covers service configuration, reverse proxies, health checks, and the troubleshooting needed to keep the pieces talking to one another.
story: A backend needs more than working endpoints. Routing, containers, database connections, certificates, and health checks all have to work together when an application leaves a development machine.

My infrastructure work includes Docker-based services, nginx and reverse proxies, Linux administration, and application troubleshooting. In lab work, I have investigated how network configuration and health checks affect service availability.
The useful part of this work is often unglamorous: isolate a failure, understand which layer owns it, make the smallest reliable fix, and check that the service behaves as expected afterwards.

projects.name: Robotics & experiments
projects.summary: Exploring the point where software meets the physical world: computer vision, voice interfaces, robotics integration, and experiments at the UDSM 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab. This is a space for prototypes and learning.
story: I chair the 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab at UDSM CoICT. The lab connects interests in software, prototyping, AI, and physical computing, with room to test ideas beyond a browser window.

My technical explorations include MediaPipe and OpenCV for webcam-based interaction, along with ideas for conversational interfaces and Swahili-language interaction. These are experiments, not finished autonomous robotics products.

Curiosity is the common thread: start with a question, build a small version, see what fails, and use that feedback to decide what to try next. The technical sketches stand in for photos and demonstrations that still need to be selected.
